---
title: "Prerequisites & Installation"
---

Complete this setup before the workshop so the hands-on sessions start smoothly. Steps are the same on macOS and Windows except where noted.

## Prerequisites

Working knowledge of Python (functions, dictionaries, f-strings) and basic familiarity with Jupyter notebooks. No prior experience with agents, MCP, or A2A is assumed.

Your machine needs:

| Requirement | Notes |
|-------------|-------|
| VS Code | With the Python and Jupyter extensions |
| Miniconda | To create an isolated Python 3.12 environment |
| Node.js | Required by some MCP tooling |
| Git | To clone the materials |
| An OpenVPN-compatible client | For the training-room LLM gateway (see below) |

## Installation

### 1. Install VS Code

::: {.panel-tabset}

## macOS

Download the macOS installer from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/), open the `.zip`, and drag `Visual Studio Code.app` into **Applications**.

## Windows

Download the Windows installer (`.exe`) from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/) and run it. On the setup screen, check **"Add to PATH"** so `code` works from the terminal.

:::

Then add these extensions in either OS (Extensions panel, or `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+X`):

- **Python** (Microsoft)
- **Jupyter** (Microsoft)

### 2. Install Miniconda

::: {.panel-tabset}

## macOS

Download the macOS installer (`.pkg`, Apple Silicon or Intel as appropriate) from the [Miniconda docs](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html) and run it. Then open a **new** Terminal window so `conda` is picked up.

## Windows

Download the Windows installer (`.exe`) from the [Miniconda docs](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html) and run it. During setup, it's fine to leave "Add Miniconda3 to PATH" unchecked — instead, use the **Anaconda Prompt** (installed alongside Miniconda) for all commands below, or select the "Python (Miniconda3)" terminal profile in VS Code.

:::

### 3. Clone the materials

::: {.panel-tabset}

## macOS (Terminal)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gates-dost-asti/A2A-MCP_Training.git
cd A2A-MCP_Training
```

## Windows (Anaconda Prompt)

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/gates-dost-asti/A2A-MCP_Training.git
cd A2A-MCP_Training
```

:::

### 4. Create the conda environment

The commands are identical on both platforms — just run them in Terminal on macOS or Anaconda Prompt on Windows:

```bash
conda create -n a2a-mcp-training python=3.12
conda activate a2a-mcp-training
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

::: {.callout-note}
`requirements.txt` is still being finalized and may change before the workshop — re-run `pip install -r requirements.txt` if you're told it's been updated.
:::

### 5. Register the environment with Jupyter

```bash
python -m ipykernel install --user --name a2a-mcp-training
```

Then pick the `a2a-mcp-training` kernel when opening any workshop notebook in VS Code or JupyterLab.

### 6. Install Node.js

::: {.panel-tabset}

## macOS

Download the macOS LTS installer (`.pkg`) from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/) and run it.

## Windows

Download the Windows LTS installer (`.msi`) from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/) and run it, keeping the default options (including "Add to PATH").

:::

Verify on either OS:

```bash
node -v
```

## Connecting to the LLM gateway

The notebooks call language models through a local helper (`gates_openai.py`) that talks to an OpenAI-compatible gateway on the training network. During the workshop:

1. Import the VPN profile provided by the facilitators into your OpenVPN-compatible client and connect.
2. Verify connectivity by running the first few cells of any notebook — the sanity-check calls should return text.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Running the notebooks outside the training room

The gateway is only reachable through the training VPN. To run the materials at home, edit `BASE_URL` in the track's `gates_openai.py` to point at your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint (for example, the official OpenAI API with your API key, or a local server such as Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint).
:::

## Quick self-check

Run this after setup; every import should succeed silently.

```python
import openai, mcp, a2a, arxiv, tavily, wikipediaapi, pydantic, nest_asyncio
print("Setup OK")
```
